content.title: Close-Threat Contact Chain | Strike Units, Escape Objective, Corridor Pursuit
content.summary: A greenhouse guard leaves a close mannequin duel when a larger group activates. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.

quick_start.input_format: One adult and one close threat are established before contact. + Each combat unit has a readable beginning, contact and displacement. + No new action begins before the previous result is visible. + Threat multiplication visibly changes the objective to escape. + The same route axis carries the final pursuit.
quick_start.recommended_input: Place one adult greenhouse guard with a padded blue pole before one malfunctioning training mannequin. Let each contact move the mannequin clear of a marked floor square before the next begins. Track the same guard retreating toward camera along the greenhouse center lane while the group follows behind.
required_anchors: One adult and one close threat are established before contact.
Each combat unit has a readable beginning, contact and displacement.
Threat multiplication visibly changes the objective to escape.
The same route axis carries the final pursuit.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: A greenhouse guard leaves a close mannequin duel when a larger group activates. Preserve the five causal invariants and terminal proof while replacing every source-specific surface.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.

not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
